title: A 0.85 degree C threshold gave 41% excess Alerts in a perfect-SST CRW rule test at 152 reef cells, 2019-2025
abstract: We audit a published cause test of excess NOAA Coral Reef Watch Alert forecasts. The test uses weekly medians, but NOAA documents a maximum of daily levels for Version 5. We compare these operators with perfect observed SST at 152 reef cells, 583 OISST pixels and 329 weekly issues in 2019-2025. At weeks 9-20, the published heat ramp gives observed/expected Alert 1+ counts of 0.286 with medians and 0.254 with maxima. Thus the large rule-only excess survives the version correction. A proposed 0.85 degree C final heat threshold gives 4.4% excess expected Alerts with medians but 41.2% with maxima (95% issue-block interval 35-48%). The maximum-rule excess remains at weeks 15-20, outside initialization-transition memory. We prove that a fixed 1 degree C threshold with a weekly maximum exactly matches satellite Alert events under perfect SST and a common baseline. The numerical test passes that identity. Weekly maxima also remove the perfect-SST Watch deficit attributed to the median rule. These results revise the proposed correction and the Watch explanation, while preserving the broad heat-ramp finding. Limitations include a cell-mean baseline, a fixed reef sample, OISST instead of 5 km satellite truth, and no real forecast ensemble. This is a paired rule test, not an operational repair or a new test of issued probabilities.

display.caption: A paired perfect-SST test of weekly medians and maxima. O/E is observed Alert 1+ count divided by expected count. Both operators use the same SST, baseline and heat ramp.
